  • $250 threshold per Aitkin fact sheet differs from $100 stated by state; verify

Who runs property tax in Aitkin County?

Responsibility is split. One office sets the value and class of each parcel, and another sends the bills and takes payment. The Assessor's Office answers at 218-927-7327. The Treasurer is at 307 2nd St NW, Room 119, Aitkin, MN 56431, and takes calls at 218-927-7325.

The Assessor's page says market value and classification are the main inputs to a tax bill, and that the office works under Minnesota statutes, Department of Revenue directives and County Board directives. A free parcel viewer called LINK shows basic parcel data. More detailed building records, including dimensions and sales reports, need a paid subscription, which the Assessor can explain by phone.

A seller here will end up talking to both: the Assessor about value and class, and the Treasurer about any balance on the parcel before the deed is signed.

What does the Aitkin County housing market look like?

Aitkin County sits in east central Minnesota and its seat is the city of Aitkin. Total area is 1,995 square miles, with 174 of them water. The Mississippi River flows south through the west central part, the terrain is wooded rolling hills, and Savanna Portage State Park and Rice Lake National Wildlife Refuge are among the protected areas on the map.

The first version of the county dates to 1857, when it carried the name Aiken, and the current spelling came in 1872. Its namesake, William Alexander Aitken, traded furs for the American Fur Company, and local government was organized in 1871. January lows in the city of Aitkin average about 0 degrees Fahrenheit, with a recorded extreme of minus 47 in 1972.

Census QuickFacts figures worth knowing before you price a house here:

  • Population of 16,252 as of July 2025, about 8.6 people per square mile of land
  • 14,681 housing units, 85.3% lived in by their owners
  • Median value of an owned home: $255,800 (2020 to 2024 survey years)
  • Households earn a median $60,833, and 35.7% of residents are past 65
  • 214 building permits in 2025, plus a 27.7 minute average drive to work

Owners dominate, and the older age profile is worth keeping in mind if the house you are selling belonged to a relative.

Is Aitkin County inspecting properties for 2027?

Yes, in a set of areas. A 2027 reassessment is listed on the Assessor's page, with appraisers on the road since May 2026. An inspection can land anywhere from May 2026 to February 2027, so one may still be ahead.

The areas on the list are Ball Bluff, Balsam, Fleming, Hazelton, Jevne, Macville, Malmo and Turner townships, unorganized territories 51-22, 52-24 and 52-25, and the city of Hill City. The county explains that this is a physical inspection used to check and fix its records, and that state law calls for it on all taxable property at least every five years.

Owners who want to be there for the walk-through can phone 218-927-7327, and the office also asks to hear about any hazards to avoid on the land. Keep receipts for recent repairs handy if you are in one of these areas.

How do I appeal an Aitkin County valuation or classification?

The county's appeals page sets a sequence, and the first step is a phone call:

  • Contact the Assessor's Office and have the front and back of your valuation notice in front of you.
  • Next comes the local board of appeal, staffed by the township board or city council, or an Open Book session if that is what your notice lists. At Open Book, the assessors review the case and decide, and that decision can still go to the county board.
  • After that is the county board, which meets in June. You schedule a time through the County Assessor, and the local step comes first unless your area has no local board.
  • The last stop is the Minnesota Tax Court, which the county says accepts petitions even from owners who skipped the earlier steps. Its deadline is April 30 of the taxes-payable year.

Statute 274.01 puts local board meetings in April and May and caps their combined reductions at one percent of the assessor's total. Under 278.01, an owner may instead serve a petition on the county auditor and file it in district court.

What are the Aitkin County tax due dates?

Bills come in two installments, one in mid-May and one in mid-October. These are the points that matter for an Aitkin County parcel:

Payment rules for Aitkin County parcels (Treasurer FAQ and Statute 279.01)
ItemWhat applies
First halfDue before May 16
Second halfDue before October 16, with no second-half statement mailed
Mailed paymentOn time when the postmark shows the due date or earlier
Late penalty after the due date2% on homestead, 4% on nonhomestead
Delinquent statusTax still unpaid when the new year begins
Delinquent listPrinted in the newspaper each March

The Treasurer does not mail second-half statements, so keep the stub from the first one. Missing paperwork is no defense: the office says the owner is still responsible, and courtesy letters for unpaid current-year tax carry added penalty and fees. After the first jump, the statute adds one percent per month, up to 8% on homestead and 12% on nonhomestead land.

Under the same statute, a tax of $100 or less is due in one payment with the first half. Owners of small parcels should ask the Treasurer which threshold applies before paying.

Who pays what when an Aitkin County house sells?

On this point the Treasurer's FAQ is direct: delinquent taxes get paid at closing. The closing statement, or the realtor or attorney on the deal, will show how the current year is divided.

Escrow customers have a lender that receives the figures straight from the county. The copy mailed to the owner says in bold print not to pay, yet it remains useful at filing time and for refund claims. A buyer who closes after statements went out can get a copy online or from the Treasurer, and the county says that is the buyer's job.

Two state rules touch the deed itself. Statute 272.115 requires a certificate of value on sales above $3,000 and has the assessor remove homestead status after a sale unless the buyer applies and qualifies. Statute 287.21 sets the deed tax at 0.33% of net consideration above that figure.

A mobile home is handled separately. Its title cannot move until the taxes are paid, and relocating one takes a Mobile Home Clearance Sheet from the Treasurer.

Can Aitkin County homeowners get tax relief?

Two programs appear in the Treasurer's FAQ. The state property tax refund is claimed on form M1PR, available from the Department of Revenue.

The second is the Senior Citizen Property Tax Deferral. The county calls it a low-interest loan from the state and says it is not tax forgiveness. Homeowners aged 65 or older with household income of $60,000 or less can defer part of the tax, the state pays the county, and interest accrues. A seller already in the program should ask the Department of Revenue how a sale affects the deferred balance before listing.

If you cannot tell whether either program fits, the Treasurer at 218-927-7325 can say what to bring.

More questions about Aitkin County, MN Property Tax Guide

Which office answers questions on an Aitkin County tax bill?

The Treasurer, at 218-927-7325, handles billing, payments and statement copies, from an office at 307 2nd St NW, Room 119. For value or class questions, dial the Assessor at 218-927-7327.

Does Aitkin County accept mailed tax payments?

Yes. A payment counts as timely if the postmark meets the due date. Address it to the Treasurer at 307 2nd St NW, Room 119, Aitkin, MN 56431. The back of each stub has a form for changing the mailing address.

What if my Aitkin County tax statement never arrives?

You still owe the tax and the same penalties apply. A replacement copy can be printed online or requested from the Treasurer.

Must back taxes be cleared to close an Aitkin County sale?

Yes, delinquent taxes are paid at closing. Tax left unpaid into the next calendar year is delinquent, so ask the Treasurer for a payoff amount well ahead of the closing date.

Is there a way to contest value after the spring boards adjourn?

Yes, by petitioning the Minnesota Tax Court before April 30 of the taxes-payable year. The Assessor's appeals page says the court hears owners who never went to the local or county board.

Which Becker County offices run property tax?

Becker County divides the job between the Assessor and the Auditor-Treasurer. The Assessor is appointed by the County Board of Commissioners and approved by the Minnesota Commissioner of Revenue. That office supervises the assessments of every township and city in the county and keeps records on about 29,200 taxable properties and 3,339 tax-exempt ones.

Appraisal work is done by state accredited and certified staff from the county office, along with certified assessors hired by townships and cities. The Auditor-Treasurer, an elected official, calculates rates, prepares statements and Truth in Taxation notices, collects the tax and county special assessments, and tracks unpaid parcels. Most Assessor records are public, apart from data covered by the privacy act.

What is the Becker County housing market like?

Becker County lies in northwest Minnesota, with Detroit Lakes as the county seat. It covers 1,445 square miles, of which 130 are water, making it the 15th largest Minnesota county by area. Several hundred lakes, farmland and forest share the landscape, among them Detroit Lake, Lake Sallie, Lake Maud, Lake Melissa and Big Cormorant Lake. The highest point is a hill near Wolf Lake at 1,861 feet.

The county was created on March 18, 1858 and organized in 1871. It carries the name of George Loomis Becker, one of three men elected to Congress at statehood. Minnesota could send only two, so Becker stayed behind and was promised a county. Colonel George Johnston founded Detroit Lakes in 1871 and the Northern Pacific Railroad fueled its early growth. An 1877 vote made Detroit the seat over Frazee, Lake Park and Audubon, and the Soo Line built through the county in 1903.

Census QuickFacts for the housing market:

  • 35,497 residents in July 2025, with 26.8 people per square mile of land
  • 20,440 housing units, and 77.2% of homes lived in by the owner
  • Median value of $291,000 for an owned home, with median rent at $920
  • Monthly owner costs of $1,691 with a mortgage and $580 without
  • 182 building permits in 2025, and retail sales of $21,864 per person in 2022

One in four residents is 65 or older, and 7.2% identify as American Indian or Alaska Native, and White Earth is among the county's census-designated places.

What does the Becker County assessment calendar look like?

The Assessor's timeline page lists duties through the year. The dates below are the ones a homeowner is most likely to need.

  • January 2 is the assessment date for real and personal property.
  • February 1 is the last day to file for exemption from taxation.
  • March 31: statements go out by this date from the Treasurer, except for manufactured homes.
  • April 1 to May 31: local boards of appeal and equalization hold their meetings, and value notices go out at least ten days ahead.
  • April 30: last day to file a Tax Court petition about current taxes.
  • June: the County Board of Appeal and Equalization meets during the last ten meeting days after the second Friday, with times printed on the valuation notice.
  • August 15: deadline for the Property Tax Refund, Form M-1PR.
  • Late November: Truth in Taxation notices go out, with public hearings in the weeks after.

December 1 is the last day for owners of real property to establish homestead for the year, though applications can be filed with the Assessor until December 15 to count for that year's assessment.

When are Becker County property taxes due?

Most owners pay in two installments, May 15 and October 15, but the county's own schedule lists several exceptions that depend on property class.

Becker County schedule of property taxes payable, by class and date (Auditor-Treasurer schedule)
DateWho it covers
May 15First half of real property tax; personal property tax
May 31First half for class 1c and 4c resorts and qualifying class 3a seasonal commercial property

Statute 279.01 adds two details. When the statements miss an April 25 postmark, the first installment moves to 21 days after the postmark date. Class 3a seasonal property qualifies for the later date only if the owner attaches an affidavit showing more than 60 percent of gross income comes from May through August.

A homestead owner on federal active service as a National Guard or reserve member gets four extra months, moving a May 15 payment to September 15 and an October 15 payment to February 15, with a copy of orders or form DD214.

How do I pay Becker County property tax online?

The Auditor-Treasurer's page links to an online and phone payment service, and e-check or card payments through it carry extra fees. The county asks for specific identifiers so the payment is credited to the right parcel.

  • Bill number: five digits, leaving off the beginning zero, printed on the first-half and second-half stubs.
  • Parcel or property ID: all nine digits with no decimal points, so 01.0001.000 is entered as 010001000.
  • Jurisdiction code: 3308 identifies Becker County.

The same page offers a parcel and tax record search showing taxes, assessments, and land and building features, linked to the county's online mapping. Run it before you list to review the taxes and assessments on record for your parcel.

What is the Becker County appeal route?

Begin with the Assessor, because a conversation about the value notice often resolves a data error. If it does not, the local board is the next step. Statute 274.01 makes the town board or city council the local board unless the city has a charter board or has handed the job to the county. Someone who ignores a notice that the board plans to raise the assessment generally cannot go to the county board later.

The county board convenes in June. After that, a petition to district court or Tax Court under Statute 278.01 must be on file by April 30 of the taxes-payable year. Appeals of manufactured homes assessed as personal property run on a separate calendar, with a September 1 petition date.

What happens to Becker County taxes when I sell?

The Auditor-Treasurer touches the sale before the Recorder does. That office collects the state deed tax, mortgage registration tax and split fees on conveyances and enters each transfer in a permanent database before the document is filed with the County Recorder. Questions on the electronic certificate of real estate value go to the Assessor's chief deputy.

Unpaid tax carries consequences beyond penalties. The Auditor-Treasurer puts delinquent parcels into judgment, runs forfeiture proceedings and sales under statute, and may use revenue recapture to collect. A seller with a back balance should settle it before closing instead of leaving it for the buyer's title company to find.

A few programs affect timing. Senior citizens apply for the state's property tax deferral by July 1 for taxes payable the following year, and farmland owners file for Green Acres deferral by May 1. Resort owners declare class 1c or 4c status with the Assessor by January 15, and people who are blind or permanently and totally disabled apply to the Department of Revenue for the special homestead class by October 1.

More questions about Becker County, MN Property Tax Guide

Who is the Becker County Assessor appointed by?

The County Board of Commissioners appoints the Assessor, and the Minnesota Commissioner of Revenue approves the appointment. The office supervises assessments for all townships and cities in the county.

When is the second Becker County property tax payment due?

October 15 for non-farm real property. Second-half tax on farm real property, including split-class parcels that are partly agricultural, is due November 15, as is the second half for manufactured homes.

Do Becker County resorts pay property tax on a different date?

Yes, the schedule differs for them. Class 1c and 4c resort property and qualifying class 3a seasonal commercial property may pay the first half by May 31 instead of May 15, per the county schedule and Statute 279.01.

What do I need to pay Becker County taxes online?

You need the five-digit bill number from your payment stub, the nine-digit parcel number without decimal points, and the jurisdiction code 3308. E-check and card payments add fees.

Where do I send questions about a Becker County eCRV?

Contact the Chief-Deputy Assessor, who the county lists for tax estimates, agricultural questions and eCRV inquiries. The County Assessor handles exempt questions and sales inquiries.

Itasca County by the numbers

Where do I deal with property tax in Itasca County?

Both the Assessor and the Auditor/Treasurer work out of the Itasca County Courthouse at 123 NE 4th Street in Grand Rapids, ZIP 55744, with weekday hours that end at 4:30 in the afternoon. The Auditor/Treasurer is on the second floor.

The Assessor finds, lists and values every taxable parcel, calculates net tax capacity by property class, mails owners their value and classification, and holds the local and county boards of equalization. The Auditor/Treasurer sends statements and takes payment. The Assessor's phone is 218-327-2861 and the Treasurer's is 218-327-2860.

What sets Itasca County apart from a typical Minnesota county?

Itasca County is a big, wooded, lake country in the Iron Range region, with Grand Rapids as the county seat. It is Minnesota's third-largest county by area: 2,928 square miles in all, 2,668 of them land.

Wikipedia counts more than 1,400 lakes, including Lake Winnibigoshish, Pokegama Lake, Deer Lake and Bowstring Lake, plus the Mississippi River, which crosses the county. Forests of pine, spruce, hardwood, cedar and tamarack cover much of it, and forestry and logging remain major parts of the local economy. Part of the Chippewa National Forest lies inside the county, as do parts of the Bois Forte and Leech Lake reservations.

For July 2025 the Census Bureau estimates 45,404 residents, a gain of just 0.9% on the 2020 base, spread over a land area of 2,667.74 square miles. That works out to 16.9 people per square mile. Residents skew older here: 27.7% are 65 or over.

  • Housing units: 26,005 in July 2025, with 249 building permits in 2025.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 83.0%, 2020 to 2024.
  • Typical owner-occupied home: $225,200 at the median.
  • Median household income: $68,603, and median gross rent: $988.

The 2020 census recorded 25.2% of Itasca housing units as vacant, the highest share among the four counties in this series.

How is Itasca County organized, and does it change who values my house?

Itasca's boundaries were first set in 1849 when Minnesota Territory was created, and the county once covered land that is now Cook, Lake, Koochiching and parts of several others. It takes its name from Lake Itasca, the source of the Mississippi, though that lake is outside today's borders.

Today the county is divided into dozens of townships, among them Bigfork, Bowstring, Deer River, Grand Rapids, Marcell, Nashwauk, Trout Lake and Wawina, plus unorganized territories. Because the Assessor's page says the county office handles valuation for all taxable property in Itasca County, a seller in a far-flung township still starts at the courthouse in Grand Rapids for value and classification questions. Where a city assessor also works in your area, the statute says the county assessor forwards a petition copy to that authority, so ask which office issued your notice.

When are Itasca County property taxes due?

A residential bill splits into May 15 and October 15 payments. Resorts, manufactured homes and agricultural land keep their own dates, and a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday pushes any of them to the following business day.

Itasca County payment due dates
Due dateTax type
May 15Real property, first half (or whole bill if $100 or less)
May 31Real property, resorts, first half
August 31Manufactured homes, first half (or whole bill if $50 or less)
October 15Real property, second half
November 15Agricultural real property and manufactured homes, second half

Source: Itasca County Payment Due Dates. Personal property and severed mineral interest taxes come due with the real property tax.

How can I pay an Itasca County tax bill?

You can pay by mail, online, by phone or in person. The county site says cash, check and debit or credit card are taken at the office, and a mailed check needs a postmark no later than the due date.

  • Card payments carry a 2.25% service fee with a $1.00 minimum.
  • An e-check through MuniciPay is a flat $1.00 per transaction under $100,000.
  • Phone payments go through 218-535-7880 and need the Property ID Number from the top left of the statement.
  • Online and phone payments take one to two business days to post.

The county also offers free automatic payment enrollment, with the same $1.00 ACH fee. If your taxes are in a mortgage escrow, the statement carries a note not to pay, and any change in the escrow agent has to come from the escrow company to the Auditor/Treasurer.

What does Minnesota add for late payment?

A missed installment draws a penalty of 2% on a homestead and 4% on anything else, per Minnesota Statutes section 279.01. A second step of the same size follows on the first of the next month, and one percent more is added monthly through December.

Caps apply at 8% for homestead and 12% for nonhomestead property. Agricultural homestead and certain rural land get a break on the second half only: no penalty attaches if it is paid by November 15. The same statute lets the county treasurer waive a penalty once when a mailed payment carries a postmark within one business day of the due date. Cabins and seasonal recreational property that are not used commercially get the homestead penalty rates, which matters in a county with this many lake properties.

How do I challenge an Itasca County valuation?

Talk to the Assessor first, then the local board in your city or township, then the county board. The Assessor's page describes this review as the first stage of appeals, with the Assessor appearing in tax court when needed.

If you still disagree, Minnesota Statutes section 278.01 lets you petition the district court by serving the county auditor and filing with the court administrator no later than April 30 of the tax-payable year. A Tax Court appeal is also open between receipt of the valuation notice and May 1. If a change in value or class reaches an owner only after February 28, the clock is 60 days counted from the day the notice was mailed.

The Assessor's page notes that the local board information was last updated on April 17, 2020, so call 218-327-2861 for this year's meeting schedule instead of relying on old postings.

What should an Itasca County seller do about taxes before closing?

Get a current statement or payoff from the Auditor/Treasurer for your parcel, and confirm whether the first and second halves of the current year are both paid. The county has its own parcel information system and an online statement lookup.

A house that sits at a lake, on forest land or in a township far from Grand Rapids may carry special assessments, so the county office is the place to confirm every line before a closing date is set. When a house is inherited, empty or behind on taxes, bring the parcel number and the latest statement and ask what is owed through the date you expect to close.

More questions about Itasca County, MN Property Tax Guide

When is the Itasca County first half due?

May 15 for regular real property. Resorts have until May 31 for the first half, and weekend or holiday dates roll forward.

What is the card fee for paying Itasca County taxes?

2.25% of the payment, with a $1.00 minimum. An e-check through the county's online service is a flat $1.00 per transaction under $100,000.

Where is the Itasca County Assessor?

In the Itasca County Courthouse at 123 NE 4th Street, Grand Rapids, MN 55744. Weekday hours run to 4:30 p.m., and the phone is 218-327-2861.

When is the court deadline to contest an Itasca County tax?

April 30 of the tax-payable year for a district court petition under Minnesota Statutes section 278.01. A Tax Court appeal can begin earlier, between the valuation notice and May 1.

Do manufactured homes in Itasca County follow the same calendar?

No. Manufactured homes pay the first half August 31 (or the whole bill if it is $50 or less) and the remainder November 15.

Mower County by the numbers

Which Mower County offices handle a property tax bill?

Two county offices share the work in Austin, and both sit in the Government Center at 201 1st Street NE. The Auditor-Treasurer in Suite 7 collects the money and is reachable at 507-437-9535. The Assessor in Suite 10 sets value and class and answers at 507-437-9440, Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM.

The Auditor-Treasurer page says the office collects real estate, personal property and mobile home taxes, then pays out each school district, city, township and special taxing district its share. The same desk collects special assessments that cities and townships levy for water, sewer, sidewalk, curb and gutter, septic and ditch repair.

Mower County runs what its Assessor calls a "true county assessor" system. County appraisers, not city or township assessors, value all of the roughly 21,300 parcels each year. That means one phone number covers every address in the county, from Austin to the smallest township.

What should a seller know about the county before pricing a house?

Mower County sits on the Iowa line in southeast Minnesota. Austin is both the county seat and largest city, and the county was created in 1855 and organized in 1856. It holds 14 cities and 20 townships laid out as a grid, five townships wide and four deep. The Cedar River crosses the western townships, and the Upper Iowa River starts here. Mower is one of only four Minnesota counties with no natural lakes, so waterfront premiums rarely come into play.

Census QuickFacts figures for the county:

  • 40,971 residents as of July 2025, up 2.3% from the April 2020 base
  • 17,120 housing units, with 77.6% lived in by their owners
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $185,200 (2020 to 2024 estimates)
  • Median gross rent of $927 and 2.52 people per household
  • Median household income of $73,074, and 136 building permits recorded in 2025

At a median under $200,000, a fixed repair bill or a back-tax balance takes a larger share of the sale price than it would in a county with higher values. Austin Municipal Airport sits east of the city, and Lake Louise State Park lies near Le Roy in the southeast corner.

Why would a Mower County appraiser come to my door?

Several routine programs put appraisers on the road, according to the Assessor's page. Appraisers wear reflective vests and drive county-branded vehicles, and they leave a card if nobody is home.

  • A five-year review of every parcel, normally run between May and September
  • Building permit reviews, done twice a year in November and January
  • Tax abatement inspections on new homes, required by the county's abatement policy
  • Reports of damaged or destroyed buildings, which owners are asked to call in so a structure that is gone stops being valued
  • Value appeals during April to June, which usually call for a full inspection of the property

Because November is a permit month, a recent addition or finished basement may already be on the appraiser's list. The county also hosts a free online parcel viewer that opens a two-page property card, tax statements and value notices for any parcel, searchable by parcel number, name or address.

How do I appeal my Mower County value?

Start with a call to your appraiser before the board date, because the Assessor says a full inspect is normally required to appeal. The 2026 notice, mailed in spring, set the value for taxes payable in 2027, and the spring meetings have now passed. The order matters next year:

  • Local board first. A township board hears appeals in the township, and the county's published April schedule had meetings from April 13 to 16, 2026. The county states you must appeal to the local board before the county board.
  • Open book instead of a meeting. Cities and some townships use open book, run in person or by phone at the Assessor's Office from April 6 to May 31, 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM. Austin city open book goes through the main office line.
  • County Board of Appeal and Equalization. It meets after the second Friday in June, made up of the County Board and the Auditor, and can change value or classification for the current year.
  • Minnesota Tax Court or district court. Under Minnesota Statutes 278.01, the petition must be filed by April 30 of the year the tax is payable.

Only the estimated market value for the current assessment year is appealable, not the tax bill itself. Local boards also work under section 274.01, which caps their combined reductions at 1% of the assessor's total.

When are Mower County property taxes due and what are the penalties?

Taxes come due in two halves, mid-May and mid-October, with a later November date for qualifying farm land. The table below puts the deadlines and the late charges together.

First halfPaid before May 16

Ceiling after monthly additions8% homestead, 12% nonhomestead
Bills of $100 or lessWhole amount due with the first half

A mailed check is on time when the envelope is postmarked by the due date. A first-time late mailer who postmarks within one business day of the deadline can ask the treasurer to abate the penalty.

What happens if the tax is unpaid when I sell?

Unpaid current-year tax becomes delinquent on January 2 of the following year, according to the Auditor-Treasurer. First-year delinquent owners are notified, and the list appears in the newspaper each March while interest keeps running. Call 507-437-9456 for a payoff figure, since the office says the posted delinquent list may lag behind the current month.

After three years of non-payment a parcel can forfeit to the State of Minnesota. The office sends a Notice of Expiration of Redemption with a last chance to pay, and forfeited parcels are later sold at a county auction. Selling before that point is usually simpler than any redemption.

At transfer, Minnesota Statutes 272.12 has the county auditor check for delinquent tax on the land. The recorder will refuse the deed unless the auditor has marked it with the words "no delinquent taxes and transfer entered." A seller in Mower County who owes back tax therefore has to clear it at or before closing.

More questions about Mower County, MN Property Tax Guide

Who do I call in Mower County to pay or ask about a tax bill?

Call the Auditor-Treasurer at 507-437-9535, or 507-437-9456 for delinquent balances. The office is in Suite 7 of the Government Center, 201 1st Street NE, Austin. Questions about value or class go to the Assessor at 507-437-9440.

Does Mower County mail a valuation notice every year?

Yes, the county values all parcels annually and mails a Notice of Valuation and Classification each spring. The notice lists your local board or open book dates. Read both sides before calling your appraiser.

Can I appeal my Mower County property tax directly to the county board?

Not in most cases. The county says you must go to the local board of appeal first, unless your city or township uses open book, in which case the County Board is the next step. The Tax Court is open at any time before April 30.

Will an appraiser inspect my Mower County home before I sell?

Possibly. Five-year reviews run from May to September, permit checks happen in November and January, and appeals usually require a full inspection. Call 507-437-9440 if a card was left on your door.

What does the county do with parcels that stay unpaid for years?

Delinquent parcels are listed each March, and after three years of non-payment they can forfeit to the State of Minnesota. The county then holds a public auction so the land returns to the tax rolls. Owners get a Notice of Expiration of Redemption before that happens.

Which Dodge County offices deal with property tax?

Two desks at the Government Services Building in Mantorville handle most questions: Land Records (the assessor) for value and classification, and Finance for the tax bill and payments. Both sit at 721 Main Street North, Mantorville, MN 55955, and the county posts weekday hours from eight in the morning until four-thirty.

  • Assessor (Land Records): 507-635-6245, Dept. 102. Ask here about estimated market value, classification, homestead and the appeal steps.
  • Finance: 507-635-6240, Dept. 45. Ask here about amounts due, duplicate statements, penalties and past-due balances.

Dodge County runs its parcel and payment lookup through an online tax portal, so you can search by parcel number or street address before you call. Lost statements can be printed from the portal for years back to 2013, and Finance mails duplicates by phone request.

Where does Dodge County sit, and who lives there?

Dodge County sits in southeastern Minnesota and belongs to the Rochester metropolitan area. Kasson is the largest city, while Mantorville holds the courthouse. The other cities are Blooming Prairie (shared with Steele County), Claremont, Dodge Center, Hayfield and West Concord.

The county was organized in 1855 and named for Henry Dodge. Its courthouse, built in 1865, is described as the oldest courthouse still in use in Minnesota, and Quarries around Mantorville once supplied cut stone, and Wasioja is known for its own stone. The land is about 24 miles long and 18 miles wide, rolling and fertile, with the South Branch of the Middle Fork of the Zumbro River crossing the upper middle.

The Census Bureau counted 20,867 residents in 2020 and estimated 21,376 for July 2025. QuickFacts lists 8,773 housing units, an owner-occupied rate of 86.6 percent, a median owner-occupied value of $287,700 and household income near $95,739 at the median for 2020 to 2024. Workers spend an average of 25.9 minutes getting to their jobs. With owners in nearly nine of ten occupied homes, a listing that arrives with an unpaid tax balance or an open classification question is easy for a buyer to spot.

When are Dodge County property taxes due?

Residential real estate tax is split into two halves, due May 15 and October 15, and farm land gets until November 15 for the second half. Minnesota law (Minn. Stat. 279.01) sets those dates and the penalties, so the county cannot waive them on its own.

The county reminds owners that a mailed payment needs a postmark dated no later than the due date. Its suggestion is to walk the envelope into the post office and ask for a hand stamp. A homestead payment that misses its date picks up 2 percent, and non-homestead picks up 4 percent. After the first of the next month the penalty climbs again, and from then on it adds 1 percent each month through December, up to a cap of 8 percent for homestead and 12 percent for non-homestead property. The state also lets the treasurer abate a first late penalty when a payment was mailed and postmarked within one business day of the deadline.

Dodge County property tax calendar. Sources: Dodge County Land Records important dates page; Minn. Stat. 279.01.
DateWhat happens
January 2Assessment date; unpaid prior-year tax becomes delinquent
March 31Last day Finance mails real estate tax statements
April 30Last day to file a Minnesota Tax Court petition for the current tax
May 15First half due
October 15Second half due, including special assessments
November 15Second half due on farm real property
December 1 and 15Own and occupy by December 1, apply for homestead by December 15

How do I pay a Dodge County tax bill?

You can pay by mail, at the Administration window, in a drop box, or online. Checks and money orders go to Dodge County, and the stub from your statement should travel with the payment. Mail goes to Dodge County Finance, 721 Main Street North, Dept. 45, Mantorville, MN 55955.

  • In person: Administration window on the main floor, paid by cash, money order, cashier's check or personal check.
  • Drop box: left of the west-facing main entrance. Write a note on the envelope if you want a receipt.
  • Online: card payments carry a 2.75 percent fee, and an e-check costs $3.99 per transaction. Plan on one to two business days for posting.

Finance sends no reminders. Only one statement per parcel goes out each year, and if you have not seen yours by April 10 the county asks you to call for a duplicate. Not receiving a statement does not remove the penalty.

How do I contest a Dodge County valuation?

Start with an appraiser at the assessor's office as soon as your spring Notice of Valuation and Classification arrives, because the assessor can change a value only until the local board convenes. After that, relief comes only from a board or the Tax Court.

  1. Local Board of Appeal and Equalization or open book meeting. Your city or township holds one in April or May, and the notice prints the date. Its reductions cannot lower the assessor's total for the district by more than one percent (Minn. Stat. 274.01).
  2. County Board of Appeal and Equalization. It meets in June. Only owners who appealed at the first level can be heard.
  3. Minnesota Tax Court. The petition is due April 30 of the year the tax is payable (Minn. Stat. 278.01). The Small Claims Division is final, while the Regular Division can be appealed further.

The county says plainly that a bill being too high is not a reason to adjust value. Bring a recent appraisal, comparable sales or errors in the property record instead. Tax-level questions belong at the December Truth in Taxation meetings.

How does homestead status work in Dodge County?

Homestead classification gives owner-occupied property a lower tax rate than similar non-homestead property. To get it, you present proof of ownership, complete an application and supply the Social Security numbers of all owners. You must also be a Minnesota resident and be listed as an owner on county tax records.

Timing matters for a buyer. A person who buys and moves in by December 1 and files by December 15 sees homestead rates in the following year's tax. A seller who rented the house out before listing may have changed the class, which is why Finance answers "why did my classification change" calls by sending people back to Land Records at 507-635-6245. Relatives of an owner can qualify too, as can certain trusts and life estates when the deed shows the interest.

How does tax get cleared when a Dodge County house sells?

The first thing the auditor checks at transfer is whether delinquent tax is owed. Under Minn. Stat. 272.12, a deed is presented to the county auditor, who looks for delinquent taxes and certifies the land clear before the recorder may accept the deed.

That is why a title company will ask for the payoff figure before closing. If you buy after statements have been mailed, Dodge County sends the new owner a courtesy letter showing the tax for the year rather than a full statement, and it does this even when a lender escrows the payment. A seller on a contract for deed stays responsible for confirming that taxes were paid, although only the new contract holder receives the bill. Ask the title or closing agent how the current year is divided between buyer and seller, since that depends on the purchase agreement.

What if back taxes are owed on a Dodge County property?

Call Finance at 507-635-6240 for the exact amount, which includes penalty and interest, or look the parcel up in the portal, where delinquent figures are kept current. Unpaid prior-year tax becomes delinquent on January 2.

Paying before listing usually simplifies the closing. If the amount is more than you can cover, ask Finance for the exact figure before the next January 2 so you know what the delinquency date will add.

Where do I send a Dodge County property tax payment?

Mail it to Dodge County Finance, 721 Main Street North, Dept. 45, Mantorville, MN 55955, with the payment stub from your statement. The postmark must carry May 15 or October 15 or an earlier date, so the county suggests having the post office hand stamp it.

Is there a fee to pay Dodge County taxes online?

Yes. Card payments carry a 2.75 percent fee and an e-check costs $3.99 per transaction, with several parcels allowed in one e-check transaction. Allow one to two business days for the payment to post.

By when must a Dodge County owner file an appeal?

The local board or open book meeting comes first, in April or May, and the date is printed on your valuation notice. A Minnesota Tax Court petition has to be filed by April 30 in the tax-payable year.

I bought a Dodge County house after statements were mailed. Do I still owe the tax?

Yes. You will receive a courtesy letter from the county instead of a statement, and the tax is still yours to pay by the due dates. Call Finance at 507-635-6240 with your parcel number or address for a copy.

Which office changes my homestead status in Dodge County?

The assessor's office in Land Records, at 507-635-6245. File in person, by phone or by email, or download the form from the county website, and apply by December 15 after owning and living in the home by December 1.

What should a seller know about Hubbard County?

Hubbard County is in northwestern Minnesota, with Park Rapids as the seat. It was created on February 26, 1883 from part of Cass County and named for Lucius Hubbard, governor from 1882 to 1887. The land is hilly, wooded and dotted with lakes, and parts of Itasca State Park, the Mississippi Headwaters and the Leech Lake Indian Reservation fall inside the county line. The cities are Akeley, Laporte, Nevis and Park Rapids.

The numbers from Census QuickFacts explain why property tax here looks different from the metro:

  • 22,369 residents in the July 2025 estimate, up 4.8% from the 2020 base.
  • 14,900 housing units but only 8,964 households, so a large share of homes are not a full-time residence. The 2020 census counted 39.6% of housing units as vacant.
  • 83.1% owner occupancy, a median home value of $282,600 and a median household income of $71,995.
  • 28.5% of residents are 65 or older.

A cabin or lake home that is used for part of the year is taxed differently from a primary residence, which is why classification is the first thing to check before listing.

Which Hubbard County office handles property tax?

Two departments share the work. The Auditor/Treasurer is responsible for property tax administration, delinquent taxes and the published delinquent tax list, and for forfeitures, repurchases and confessions of judgment. By statute the auditor also sits on the county board of equalization.

The assessor operates inside Property Records at the Government Center, 301 Court Ave., Park Rapids, MN 56470, phone 218-732-3552. Property Records covers valuation and classification, homestead, tax reduction programs and recording of real estate documents, so a single visit can cover a value question and a deed.

When are Hubbard County property taxes due and what are the penalties?

Minnesota Statutes 279.01 sets two halves, payable before May 16 and before October 16 when a parcel's tax is over $100. A parcel at or under $100 is due in full with the first half. A payment mailed and postmarked by the due date is on time, and the treasurer must abate the penalty once if the postmark falls within one business day after.

Late payment penalties under Minnesota Statutes 279.01
StageHomesteadNonhomestead
Day after the due date2%4%
First day of the next monthAnother 2%Another 4%
Each month after, through December1% more1% more
Ceiling8%12%

Agricultural homestead and qualifying farm land can pay the second half through November 15 without penalty. Seasonal residential recreational property that is not used commercially, the statute's class 4c, takes the homestead penalty rates.

How does homestead work for a Hubbard County buyer or seller?

The county has posted a homestead notice for the 2026 assessment. An owner who bought or moved into a home in the past year must apply by December 31, 2026 to have the benefit apply to taxes payable in 2027, and the applicant must have owned and lived in the home by that date. A qualifying relative living there also counts. For residential and agricultural property that list takes in the owner's or spouse's child, grandchild, sibling or parent, plus the owner's uncle, aunt, nephew or niece.

  • Applications can be filed online, in person or by mail, and once granted they are not repeated unless the assessor asks.
  • Every occupant, owner and spouse signs and gives a Social Security number so the state can check that no other Minnesota homestead is claimed.
  • The driver's license must show the home address, since Minnesota requires an address change within 30 days.
  • A relative homestead does not qualify for the property tax refund, and a property that was ever classified seasonal residential recreational under the current owner cannot take a relative homestead.

A seller who moves out or no longer qualifies has to tell the assessor within 30 days. Missing that notice can mean recalculation as nonhomestead and a penalty equal to 100 percent of the homestead benefit.

How do I dispute a Hubbard County valuation?

Talk to the assessor at 218-732-3552 first. Minnesota Statutes 274.01 then gives two stages. The local board of appeal and equalization, which is the town board or city council unless it has handed the job to the county, meets between April 1 and May 31 with at least ten days of published notice. It must finish within 20 days of convening, and its reductions cannot lower the assessor's total by more than one percent.

An owner who skips the local board, after being notified, generally cannot appear before the county board, so missing the spring meeting costs you a step. A late disagreement goes to the county board of equalization, where the auditor serves. Tax Court is the last stop, and a district court petition for a given tax year must be filed by April 30 of that year under Statutes 278.01.

What Hubbard County dates fall in the next few weeks?

  • November 15: the last day to pay the second half on qualifying agricultural property without penalty.
  • December: late penalty on unpaid halves keeps growing by 1 percent each month until it reaches the cap for the property type.
  • December 31, 2026: the final day to apply for homestead on a home you owned and lived in during the year.
  • April 30, 2027: the court filing date for a petition about taxes payable in 2027, which follows the March valuation notice.

A seller who closes before December 31 should tell the buyer about the homestead deadline, because the buyer's own application is what carries the benefit into 2027 taxes. The assessor at 218-732-3552 can mail or email the form.

What does a seller need to settle on a Hubbard County sale?

Pay any delinquent tax before recording. Hubbard's recorder asks for this in its recording guidance, and Minnesota Statutes 272.12 stops the auditor from transferring a parcel with delinquent tax on it. Current-year tax is not required at the time of recording unless the parcel is being split, and it is usually collected and paid through the closing settlement. Tax payments are not part of the electronic recording process, so the title company handles the payoff separately.

The recorder accepts abstract and Torrens documents through four trusted submitters: ePN, Indecomm Global Services, Corporation Service Company and Simplifile. State deed tax and mortgage registration tax are collected together with the recording fee. A deed uses an eCRV and, when needed, an electronic well disclosure certificate. For a payoff figure on the current year, ask the Hubbard County Treasurer's Office. Ask the assessor how a lake home is classified, since that decides which penalty rates and homestead rules apply.

Payments go to the Auditor/Treasurer at the Government Center in Park Rapids, or through the Pay Your Taxes Online link on the county's I want to Pay page. Mail must be postmarked by the due date.

Does a Hubbard County cabin qualify for homestead?

Only if you own it and live in it as your primary home, or a qualifying relative does. Seasonal residential recreational property is a separate class, and a relative homestead is barred for any property that has been classified that way under the current owner.

When must I apply for Hubbard County homestead?

By December 31, 2026 for the current assessment, which affects taxes payable in 2027. You must own and occupy the property by that date, and applications can be made online, in person or by mail.

Are Hubbard County property taxes paid at closing?

Current-year tax is not required at recording unless the parcel is being split, but it is often settled at closing. Delinquent tax must be paid before the deed is recorded.

218-732-3552, at Property Records, 301 Court Ave., Park Rapids, MN 56470. The office handles valuation, classification, homestead and recording.

What does the Lyon County Assessor do?

The Lyon County Assessor's Office sets the market value and classification of each parcel as of January 2 each year. It is at 607 West Main Street, Marshall, MN 56258.

Minnesota statutes require the assessor to inspect every property at least once in a five-year interval, and the county describes a quintile review that relies on a physical, in-person inspection to gather property characteristics. Valuation notices go out each spring, and local, county and state boards of equalization meet every year as a forum to appeal value or classification. The office also runs the Green Acres, blind or disabled homestead and local option disaster abatement programs, and takes homestead applications.

What does the Lyon County Auditor/Treasurer handle?

The Auditor/Treasurer is the county's chief financial officer and its property tax administrator, and also its chief election official. For taxes, that means calculating each bill, collecting current and delinquent real estate tax, managing escrow, settling receipts with the taxing entities, running forfeited land proceedings and handling special assessments including ditches.

By statute the Auditor/Treasurer is also a member of the County Board of Equalization. The county's online tools let you find and pay your property tax online and search property records, valuation, classification and sales information. If your parcel has ditch assessments, ask this office to itemize them.

What kind of county is Lyon County for a seller?

Lyon County has Marshall as its seat and makes up the Marshall Micropolitan Statistical Area. It covers 715 square miles of land, second only to Itasca among the four counties in this series.

The Yellow Medicine, Redwood and Cottonwood rivers cross the county on their way northeast, and the land is low rolling hills. The state legislature established the county in 1868 and 1869, naming it for Army officer Nathaniel Lyon, who was killed in the Civil War in 1861. In 1873 the western 43% became Lincoln County. Cities are Balaton, Cottonwood, Florence, Garvin, Ghent, Lynd, Marshall, Minneota, Russell, Taunton and Tracy.

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 25,684 people, only 0.6% above 2020. Lyon is the most renter-heavy of the four counties: the owner-occupied rate is 72.5% for 2020 to 2024, and the 2020 census counted 33.6% of occupied units as renter-occupied.

  • Housing units in July 2025: 11,437, with just 23 building permits in 2025.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $200,700, the lowest of the four.
  • Median gross rent: $781; median household income: $75,303.
  • Mean commute: 14.6 minutes, the shortest of the four.

What do the 2020 census and QuickFacts say about Lyon County homes and jobs?

Lyon County is more urban than the other three counties here: 53.5% of residents lived in urban areas in 2020, and the median age was 37.5. The county had 10,137 households in 11,180 housing units, with 9.3% vacant and a rental vacancy rate of 12.5%.

Census QuickFacts lists 12,732 people employed at employer establishments in 2023 across 814 establishments, and 2022 retail sales of $650.65 million, or $25,583 per resident, the highest per-person figure of the four counties. Bachelor's degree attainment is 31.1%, foreign-born residents make up 6.1%, and 11.2% of people age 5 and older speak a language other than English at home.

  • Two airports serve the county: Southwest Minnesota Regional Airport (MML) and Tracy Municipal Airport (TKC).
  • Camden State Park and Garvin State Park are inside the county, along with several state wildlife management areas.
  • The median home value of $200,700 is lower than in Isanti ($306,200) or Le Sueur ($316,500), and median gross rent is $781 a month.

When are Lyon County property taxes due?

Minnesota sets the schedule for Lyon County like every other county: half before May 16 and half before October 16 when a bill is over $100. Smaller bills are paid once, at the first-half date.

Agricultural second halfNo penalty if paid by November 15

Source: Minnesota Statutes section 279.01. One more point: the treasurer may accept a payment larger or smaller than the exact installment, and it goes first to the oldest installment still owed and to accrued penalty before tax when it falls short. A homestead owner in the National Guard or a reserve component on federal active service gets a four-month grace period with no penalty, and must send a copy of orders or form DD214 with the payment.

How do homestead applications work in Lyon County?

Fill out the homestead application online and print it, or print a blank and fill it out by hand. Return it by mail to the Lyon County Assessor's Office, 607 West Main Street, Marshall, MN 56258, or put it in the drop box at the rear entrance of the Lyon County Government Center.

One local exception: if the property is inside the City of Marshall, call 507-537-6771 to file for homestead. The county says homestead is the program it is asked about most often, and it has a plain-language FAQ on what a homestead is and why it matters. Classification matters most when a payment is late, because the penalty on a nonhomestead parcel starts at 4% instead of 2%.

The state's Homestead Credit Refund is a separate benefit from the Department of Revenue. Its due date is August 15 and it can be filed for up to one year after that date.

How can I appeal a Lyon County valuation?

Read the spring notice, call the assessor with your evidence, and then use the local, county or state board of equalization meetings the office describes if you still disagree. The Assessor's FAQ page lists each step, including what evidence to bring to the board.

If you take the matter to court, Minnesota Statutes section 278.01 says a petition must be served on the county auditor and filed with the district court administrator by April 30 of the year the tax is payable. A Tax Court appeal can begin after the valuation notice arrives and has to begin before May 1. The statute also gives an owner 60 days from the notice mailing date when a change in value or class is not announced until after February 28.

What should a Lyon County seller check before closing?

Ask the Auditor/Treasurer for the amount owed on your parcel, including penalty and any ditch or other special assessment, and compare it with your closing date. Ask the Assessor whether the homestead classification still matches how the house is used.

The Assessor's online property search shows the property record card, valuation, classification and characteristics for a parcel, and a separate tax information page shows statements and sales. Print the record card before you list, so the numbers you quote match the county's.

Lyon County Assessor's Office, 607 West Main Street, Marshall, MN 56258. There is also a drop box at the rear entrance of the Lyon County Government Center.

Who do I call to file homestead for a house inside Marshall?

Call 507-537-6771. The county says properties within the City of Marshall file through that number.

How often does the Lyon County assessor inspect a property?

At least once in a five-year interval, under Minnesota law. The county uses a quintile review that includes an on-site, in-person inspection.

What is the court deadline to challenge a Lyon County tax?

April 30 of the year the tax is payable for a district court petition. A Tax Court appeal must start before May 1, under Minnesota Statutes section 278.01.

What is the largest late penalty on a Lyon County rental?

12% of the unpaid tax, which is the cap for nonhomestead property under Minnesota Statutes section 279.01. Homestead property is capped at 8%.

What does Cook County look like to a house seller?

Minnesota's far northeastern tip belongs to Cook County, a wooded wedge pressed between Lake Superior and the Canadian line. It holds 1,452.57 square miles of land and about 5,522 people on the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate, so roughly four residents share each square mile.

  • Named places include Grand Marais, Hovland, Grand Portage, Tofte, Schroeder and Lutsen.

Buyers here are few and often seasonal, so a cabin or lakeshore lot can carry a very different tax picture from a year-round house in town. Pull your statement before you set a price.

Real estate tax comes in two halves, due May 15 and October 15, and the Assessor's calendar gives November 15 as the second-half date for agricultural land. Both 2026 real estate dates have gone by, so a balance from this year is already growing.

State law (Minnesota Statutes 279.01) adds 2% to a late homestead bill and 4% to a late nonhomestead bill right after the date, then adds more at the start of each later month, with caps of 8% and 12%. The Auditor-Treasurer can quote the exact payoff for any year.

  • If the board leaves the value standing, you can petition the Minnesota Tax Court or the district court. Section 278.01 puts the filing deadline for that petition and its proof of service at April 30 of the year the tax is payable.

The Assessor also has to inspect every property at least once in five years. The 2026 review area, tied to the January 2, 2027 assessment, covers Lutsen, Tofte and Schroeder, and inspection visits there are booked by phone.

How does a Cook County sale deal with the tax bill?

The deed will not be recorded until the auditor confirms the land has no delinquent tax. Section 272.12 has the auditor check the books and mark the deed "no delinquent taxes and transfer entered"; without that mark the recorder refuses it.

Two more items travel with a sale. Any price above $3,000 calls for a certificate of real estate value (section 272.115). A deed that carves off only part of a tax parcel also needs the treasurer's certification that the current year's tax on the full parcel is paid (section 272.121). The sale ends the seller's homestead too, since the Assessor drops the class for the next assessment year unless the buyer applies and qualifies.

Ask the Auditor-Treasurer which years are open on your parcel before you accept an offer.

Which Cook County filing dates can catch an owner off guard?

Several relief filings have fixed cutoffs. A homestead application must reach the Assessor by December 31 to count for the following year, and disabled veteran exclusion filings use the same day. Owners who are blind or permanently and totally disabled have until October 1 for the special homestead class, and a senior citizen deferral request is due July 1.

The Property Tax Refund form M-1PR is due August 15. Resort owners file a declaration by January 15, and a 2c managed forest application is due April 30. Ask the Assessor which of these apply to your parcel.

More questions about Cook County, MN Property Tax Guide

Is this the same Cook County as Chicago?

No. This page covers Cook County, Minnesota, on the north shore of Lake Superior, with Grand Marais as county seat. Its property tax offices are the Assessor at 218-387-3650 and the Auditor-Treasurer at 218-387-3640.

When is the next Cook County property tax payment due?

The 2026 halves, May 15 and October 15, are past, so the next real estate date is the first-half deadline in May 2027, for taxes payable in 2027. Agricultural land used November 15 for its second half this year. Statements are mailed on or before March 31.

Can I pay delinquent Cook County taxes online?

No. The county says delinquent taxes for prior years cannot be paid online, only current-year taxes once the amounts are calculated in late March. Call the Auditor-Treasurer at 218-387-3640 to get a payoff amount for each open year, and ask about any partial payment before you send money.

Can I still appeal my Cook County value this year?

The 2026 local and county board meetings are over. A Tax Court or district court petition on taxes payable in 2027 must be filed by April 30, 2027, and you should talk to the assessor first. Call 218-387-3650.

Do I have to pay off the tax before selling a Cook County house?

Delinquent tax must be cleared before the deed can be recorded, and the auditor stamps the deed once that is done. Ask the Auditor-Treasurer at 218-387-3640 for the amount owed on your parcel before you accept an offer.

Where do Nobles County property owners get tax answers?

The Government Center at 315 Tenth Street in Worthington houses both offices you will need. The Auditor-Treasurer answers at 507-295-5258 and takes mail at PO Box 757, Worthington, MN 56187. The Assessor is at 507-295-5208. The Auditor-Treasurer page calls that office the county's property tax administrator and a statutory member of the County Board of Equalization.

The office also handles some items that rarely appear in other counties' summaries: wind energy and transmission line taxes, ditch fund assessments, tax increment financing and mobile home transfers. For a house seller the useful pieces are collecting current and delinquent tax, special assessments and forfeiture proceedings.

The Assessor's page lists forms for homestead, general exemption, blind or disabled homestead and the disabled veteran exclusions. The homestead form is the one an owner-occupant files with this office.

What kind of county is Nobles County for a home seller?

Nobles County is in the southwest corner of Minnesota against the Iowa border, on the Buffalo Ridge, where hills reach about 1,995 feet. The county was created in 1857 and organized in 1870, with Worthington platted in 1871 and named seat in 1873. Eleven cities share the map, among them Adrian, Brewster, Ellsworth, Round Lake and Wilmont. Lake Okabena and Lake Ocheda sit in the county, and farming leads the economy, with corn, soybeans and hogs, followed by food processing and metal fabrication.

QuickFacts numbers for the county:

  • 22,338 people in July 2025, only 0.2% above the 2020 base
  • 8,417 housing units, 74.2% owner-occupied
  • Median owner-occupied value of $197,200 and median gross rent of $896
  • 2.80 people per household, and 28.6% of residents under 18
  • 38.3% Hispanic or Latino, with 34.6% of people age 5 and over speaking a language other than English at home
  • Median household income of $66,101 and 94 building permits in 2025

Carrying costs are modest by state standards: median selected monthly owner costs run $1,456 with a mortgage and $590 without one. Per-person income is $31,342, and 13.3% of residents are below the poverty line, so a large unexpected tax or assessment bill lands harder here than the headline home value suggests. The county posts local tax rates and proposed levies on its property tax page, so you can see what the next bill is built from.

When do Nobles County property taxes fall due in 2026?

The county's own 2026 calendar splits dates by property type, which is different from the single mid-October date many owners expect:

Nobles County 2026 payment calendar as posted by the Auditor-Treasurer
DateWhat is due
May 15, 2026All taxes, first half
August 31, 2026Mobile home taxes, first half
October 15, 2026City taxes, second half, if applicable
November 16, 2026Farm taxes and mobile home taxes, second half, if applicable

November 15 falls on a Sunday this year, which is why the farm date reads November 16. The second half is not mailed, so keep the first-half stub. The county processes payments within 24 hours of receipt. If you are late, call the office at 507-295-5258 to learn the penalty to include, since the state sets it under section 279.01: 2% on homestead and 4% on other property for the first missed date, rising monthly to caps of 8% and 12%.

What are the ways to pay in Nobles County?

The county lists six methods on its property tax page:

  • Mail a check payable to Nobles County Auditor-Treasurer with the stub from every parcel; the postmark must be on or before the due date
  • Direct payment plan, which pulls the amount from a checking or savings account until you cancel
  • Online by card or e-check, with convenience fees
  • In person at the Government Center by check, cash or card
  • The drop box outside the main entrance on the 10th Street side, open around the clock
  • Escrow through a mortgage lender, which applies when the lender's name appears at the top of the statement

The county will not take post-dated checks, and a private postage meter mark does not prove timely mailing. The office also reminds owners that liability for the tax stands even if a statement never arrives.

How do I contest my Nobles County valuation?

Only the estimated market value for the current assessment year can be contested, according to the Board of Appeal and Equalization handbook posted by the county, and the number is struck as of January 2. Rather than the tax amount, the board reviews the value and class behind it. Call the Assessor first to check the facts on your notice.

  1. Go to your local board, or the open book session if your area holds one. Valuation notices must be mailed at least 10 days beforehand.
  2. If the result still looks wrong, take it to the County Board of Equalization. In 2026 it met on June 16 at 6:00 PM, and the board may sit up to 10 consecutive meeting days in June after the second Friday.
  3. File with the Minnesota Tax Court or district court by April 30 of the year the tax is payable, per section 278.01.

Neither board can grant special program status, such as Green Acres. Those need their own application, and a board may not give relief to an owner who refused the assessor entry to inspect.

Which towns and neighbors border a Nobles County property?

Beyond Worthington, the county's cities are Adrian, Bigelow, Brewster, Dundee, Ellsworth, Kinbrae, Lismore, Round Lake, Rushmore and Wilmont, and Leota is a census-designated place. Org, Pfingsten, Ransom, Reading and St. Kilian are unincorporated communities. Murray, Cottonwood, Jackson and Rock counties adjoin it in Minnesota, with Osceola and Lyon counties across the line in Iowa.

The county has a long list of state wildlife management areas and county parks, among them Adrian Spring County Park, Hawkeye County Park and the Lake Bella and Fulda wildlife areas. Prairieland Transit serves the county. Where your house sits matters for the tax bill, because the school district, city or township levy on the statement changes with the address even when the county levy is the same.

What should a Nobles County seller check before closing?

Ask the Auditor-Treasurer for any balance on the parcel, since delinquent tax and unpaid special assessments surface at transfer. Under section 272.12, the auditor looks up delinquent tax when a deed arrives, and the recorder refuses a deed lacking the "no delinquent taxes and transfer entered" stamp.

The office lists tax forfeiture proceedings among its duties, and its property tax page links to a list of tax forfeiture property. Selling well ahead of that stage keeps the decision with you. If your lender collects through escrow, ask the lender how the escrow balance will be handled at payoff, and ask the Auditor-Treasurer whether the second half has been paid.

More questions about Nobles County, MN Property Tax Guide

What is the phone number for Nobles County property taxes?

Call 507-295-5258 for the Auditor-Treasurer, who collects tax. The Assessor, who sets value and class, is at 507-295-5208. Both are in the Government Center at 315 Tenth Street, Worthington.

Why is the farm tax date November 16 in 2026?

The usual agricultural date of November 15 lands on a Sunday this year. Nobles County posts November 16, 2026 for farm and mobile home second-half payments, so the deadline moves to Monday.

Does Nobles County mail second-half tax statements?

No. The county does not mail second-half statements, so you must keep the stub from the first mailing. Taxpayers remain responsible for payment even when no statement reaches them.

Can I use the drop box for a late-night payment?

Yes. The drop box outside the Government Center's main entrance on 10th Street is accessible 24 hours a day. A mailed payment instead needs a postmark on or before the due date.

Can I appeal a Nobles County tax bill amount?

You can contest the estimated market value or classification, not the tax amount itself. Start with the Assessor, then the local board or open book, then the County Board, and file any Tax Court petition by April 30.

Douglas County by the numbers

Who handles property tax in Douglas County, Minnesota?

Two offices share the work. The Assessor's Office values and classifies about 30,000 parcels, and the Auditor/Treasurer calculates, bills and collects the tax. Both are in Alexandria, and the assessor's FAQ lists county hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

  • Assessor: 305 8th Avenue West, 2nd floor, Alexandria, MN 56308. Phone 320-762-3884, email assessors.office@co.douglas.mn.us.
  • Auditor/Treasurer: 821 Cedar Street, Alexandria, MN 56308. Phone 320-762-3077, tax email taxdept@co.douglas.mn.us.

The county's Parcel Info Lookup gives you the tax statement and the value notice by parcel. Some assessment districts in Douglas County hire their own local assessor under contract, so call the county office if you want to know who actually viewed your house.

What kind of county is Douglas County for a house seller?

Douglas County is a lake county in west-central Minnesota with Alexandria as both seat and largest city. The county was created in 1858 and organized in 1866, and it is named for Stephen A. Douglas. Roughly 83 of its 720 square miles are water, with more than 250 lakes. Lake Carlos State Park is inside the county, and it holds Minnesota's only wine-grape appellation, the Alexandria Lakes AVA.

Other cities are Brandon, Carlos, Evansville, Forada, Garfield, Kensington, Millerville, Miltona, Nelson and part of Osakis. The 2020 census counted 39,006 people, and the Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 40,120.

QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 shows a median owner-occupied value of $321,400, an owner-occupied rate of 76.5 percent, a median household income of $79,043 and 17,519 households. The county had 23,040 housing units in 2025 and issued 319 building permits that year. The 2020 count of housing units showed 23.9 percent vacant, a figure that can include seasonal lake homes. That matters for sellers because the county assessor classifies seasonal residential property separately from year-round homes.

When are Douglas County property taxes due?

Real estate tax comes due in two halves, May 15 and October 15, and the county says the postmark counts. Agricultural property and mobile homes have a later second-half date of November 15, while mobile home first-half tax is due August 31.

Statements go out on or before March 31, and the proposed tax notices for the coming year are mailed in mid to late November, so a notice may already be in your mailbox this month. A missed deadline brings a 2 percent penalty on homestead and 4 percent on non-homestead property (Minn. Stat. 279.01).

Tax typeFirst paymentSecond payment

AgriculturalMay 15November 15

How can I pay my Douglas County tax bill?

The Auditor/Treasurer lists five ways to pay: an ACH direct payment plan, a drop box, online credit card or virtual check, mail, or a visit to the office. The office moved from the courthouse to the Administration Building, so older directions to the courthouse no longer apply.

  • Drop boxes: one on the west side of the Administration Building and a drive-through box in the parking lot, both at 821 Cedar Street.
  • Online: reached from the county website through the parcel lookup.
  • ACH: the county's direct payment plan debits your account on the due dates.

To have a duplicate statement mailed, call 320-762-3077. For a copy of the value notice, call the assessor at 320-762-3884.

How are Douglas County values set and what moves them?

Values are set as of January 2 each year, and sales are the main driver. The assessor compares sale prices with assessed values to check each district against state standards, then mails every owner a notice of value and classification in the spring. There are five classes: residential, seasonal, apartment, agricultural and commercial/industrial, and each property is either homestead or non-homestead.

The county's own summary for the 2024 assessment said every district would see an increase, and that lakefront was the hot segment: 114 lake sales averaged $580,000, up 17 percent, with front-foot values on the chain of lakes running between $400 and $600 depending on the lake. The same notice explains that a higher value does not by itself raise your bill. Your taxable market value is multiplied by the class rate to find your share of the levy that the county, city or township and school district have set.

The assessor's FAQ also lists what does and does not push value up. Minor repairs such as a new roof, porch repair, original siding, paint or replaced plumbing and electrical fixtures usually will not raise the estimated market value alone, although several together could. Fire or storm damage should be reported, since the assessment date is January 2.

How do I appeal a Douglas County assessment?

Call the assessor first at 320-762-3884. Formal appeals happen in order, and the June county board only hears you if the local board or open book meeting heard you first.

  1. Local board or open book. The county's 2024 notice scheduled these for April 9 through April 19, by appointment. Your valuation notice names the date and place for your district, and Alexandria has its own city board.
  2. County Board of Appeal and Equalization. This meets in June.
  3. Minnesota Tax Court. The petition is filed by April 30 of the year the tax is payable (Minn. Stat. 278.01).

Meetings cannot change the tax statement you are paying now. They only affect the next one. Owners who struggle with a homestead bill can check the state Department of Revenue's M1PR form, which compares income with property tax due and may give a partial refund.

What does it take to qualify for homestead in Douglas County?

You must occupy the property as your primary residence, be one of its owners or a relative of an owner, and be a Minnesota resident. The assessor's FAQ points to voter registration, driver's license, income tax forms and vehicle registration as records that should show the homestead address.

This is worth checking before a sale in a lake county. A cottage that a family treats as a second home is a seasonal class, and the class rate differs from a year-round homestead. If the buyer plans to live in the house, the assessor will need a fresh application from them, so give the buyer the assessor's number, 320-762-3884, early in the process.

Moving also means updating the mailing address on the tax record. Douglas County has a Taxpayer Address Change Request Form that can be emailed or mailed to the Auditor-Treasurer's Office at 821 Cedar Street, so the next statement reaches the right owner.

What happens to the tax when a Douglas County house sells?

The county auditor must see that no delinquent tax sits on the land before a deed can be recorded (Minn. Stat. 272.12). Ask the closing agent for the tax payoff before the signing date, and ask how the current half-year is divided between you and the buyer under your purchase agreement.

New buyers who want homestead need to apply, because all new homesteads require an application, and owners who live in their house but are not getting homestead status should contact the assessor. Taxes left unpaid long enough can end in forfeiture. The Auditor/Treasurer's page says forfeited property goes to the state after the redemption period ends, and that period has been three years since January 1, 2014, down from five.

More questions about Douglas County, MN Property Tax Guide

What is the Douglas County Auditor/Treasurer's phone number?

The office number is 320-762-3077, at 821 Cedar Street in Alexandria. Tax questions can also go to taxdept@co.douglas.mn.us, and the county lists regular hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Can I pay Douglas County property tax by drop box?

Yes. There is a box on the west side of the Administration Building and a drive-through box in the parking lot. The county counts the postmark as timely for mailed payments.

Do I need an appointment to appeal a Douglas County value?

Yes, the county has required appointments for local board and open book meetings. Call the assessor at 320-762-3884 or email assessors.office@co.douglas.mn.us, and call the city if you live in Alexandria and want its board.

What is the November tax notice from Douglas County?

It is the proposed tax notice for next year. The county says these are mailed in mid to late November, and they are separate from the statement you receive by March 31.

How long do I have to redeem a Douglas County parcel that went tax forfeit?

The county states a three-year redemption period, shortened from five years effective January 1, 2014. Contact the Auditor/Treasurer at 320-762-3077 before that period ends.
